en.html:
I took leave of Kuniuji, who had gone into a <ruby>state<rt>state</rt></ruby> of complete absent-mindedness, and went back to surveying the castle. One round of the southern enclosures first, then west.

On the west side the outer works are mostly fields, storehouses, factory buildings. Low importance, and therefore very <ruby>peaceful<rt>peaceful</rt></ruby>. Here one does not meet a patrol soldier's suspicious eyes every ten steps, no such botheration.

That also means, naturally, that for me it has little meaning. I went fast towards the north, where the secrets are kept. Time is gold, the brass-colored kind, but gold all the same, and wasting it is not allowed.

en.html:
Looking back, I found myself thinking so.

Kuniuji Ashikaga and Sakurako Okabe: the winner and the loser. The destroyer and the destroyed. One who ought to be hated and one who ought to hate. One boy and one girl.

Without any intention, I had been present at their meeting. The worlds they live in are far from mine, and there is nothing I can do. Still, I cannot stop myself from thinking.

Both carry too much. Considering their age, it is nothing short of cruel.

Will their meeting ease that hardship even a little, or will it be the reverse?

Let it be the former.

Forgetting my own position, I found I was wishing it so.

en.html:
I stopped on a pass road looking down on a field of flowers.

Some women were picking flowers there, squealing merrily. Not the look of lower-ranking laborers at agricultural work. These seemed to be ladies of some rank, amusing themselves.

The sight itself caught my attention first. What kept it caught was a lone figure watching them from a little distance.

Nobody else.

That was Ichijou.

　農業に従事する下級労働者の作業という趣ではない。

　しかし注意を持続させねばならなかったのは、やや

en.html: The girl watched that ordinary sight quietly. Quietly did not mean without feeling—◆and suddenly I understood: I could tell the difference at a glance now. So much had accumulated between us already. That realization moved me. In terms of time, it is not so long. But there have been opportunities far out of proportion to that length, for getting to know the human beingperson called Ichijou Ayane. A strange girl, I think. She feels manufactured・・・・・. Not like a doll, that is a different impression. The nearest I can come is to say she is like a machinemachine. A doll-like person is, first of all, empty. One senses a heart too small for the size of the vessel, so the wide surplus space is what strikes the eye. Hence: the shell of a human, a doll. Ichijou is different. She has no surplus space・・・・・・・. That heart of hers, stuck to its one idea of justice, is puny and cramped. And yet it looks proportionate・・・・・・. The girl's body exists only to hold one will, one ideal, one purpose. From the very beginning. That is not a human being. That is not a doll. It is a machine.
en.text:
The girl watched that ordinary sight quietly. Quietly did not mean without feeling—◆and suddenly I understood: I could tell the difference at a glance now. So much had accumulated between us already. That realization moved me.

In terms of time, it is not so long. But there have been opportunities far out of proportion to that length, for getting to know the human beingperson called Ichijou Ayane.

A strange girl, I think.

She feels manufactured・・・・・. Not like a doll, that is a different impression.

The nearest I can come is to say she is like a machinemachine.

A doll-like person is, first of all, empty. One senses a heart too small for the size of the vessel, so the wide surplus space is what strikes the eye. Hence: the shell of a human, a doll.

Ichijou is different.

She has no surplus space・・・・・・・.

That heart of hers, stuck to its one idea of justice, is puny and cramped. And yet it looks proportionate・・・・・・.

The girl's body exists only to hold one will, one ideal, one purpose. From the very beginning.

That is not a human being.

That is not a doll.

It is a machine.

ja.html: 少女は静かな視線をその凡庸な光景に注いでいる。 　静けさは、無感動を意味するものとは違ったけれど も――◆一見してそうと知れるほどには関係を蓄積して いるのだと不意に理解して、俺は感慨を抱いた。 　時間を云えば、まだ然程長くはない筈だが。 　長さに見合わぬ多くの機会があった。綾弥一条なる 人間ヒトを知る為の。 　あれは、奇妙な娘だと思う。 　つくりもの・・・・・めいていると、そう感じる。 　人形のよう、という印象とはまた違う。 　器械キカイのようだと言い表すのが最も近い。 　人形じみた人間は、まず第一に虚ろである。 　器の大きさに比してちっぽけな心しか感じられない から、ぽっかりと広い余剰空間が目に付くのだ。 　だから人間の抜け殻――人形だと見られる。 　 　一条は違う。 　余剰空間が無い・・・・・・・。 　正義の一念に固執するあの心は矮小にして狭小だ。 　だが、それが相応に見える・・・・・・のである。 　少女の肉体は一つの意思、一つの理念、一つの目的 を収める為だけのものなのだ。最初から。 　それは人間ではない。 　それは人形ではない。 　それは器械だ。

も――◆一見してそうと知れるほどには関係を蓄積して
いるのだと不意に理解して、俺は感慨を抱いた。

　時間を云えば、まだ然程長くはない筈だが。
　長さに見合わぬ多くの機会があった。綾弥一条なる
人間ヒトを知る為の。

　あれは、奇妙な娘だと思う。

　人形のよう、という印象とはまた違う。

　器械キカイのようだと言い表すのが最も近い。

　人形じみた人間は、まず第一に虚ろである。
　器の大きさに比してちっぽけな心しか感じられない
から、ぽっかりと広い余剰空間が目に付くのだ。

　だから人間の抜け殻――人形だと見られる。
　
　一条は違う。
　余剰空間が無い・・・・・・・。

　正義の一念に固執するあの心は矮小にして狭小だ。
　だが、それが相応に見える・・・・・・のである。

　少女の肉体は一つの意思、一つの理念、一つの目的
を収める為だけのものなのだ。最初から。
　それは人間ではない。
　それは人形ではない。

　それは器械だ。

en.html:
The thought had crossed my mind before. But only now had I put it plainly to myself. One question: was a machine unhappy?

A doll must be unhappy, surely. Shaped like a human, yet unable to become one.

But a machine? Built as a machine, functioning as a machine.

Is that unhappy?

I could not produce an answer.

Only one thing I knew. Unhappy or happy, the machine goes on performing the single function it has been given.

Until it breaks.

The thought had crossed my mind before. But only now had I put it plainly to myself. One question: was a machine unhappy?

A doll must be unhappy, surely. Shaped like a human, yet unable to become one.

But a machine? Built as a machine, functioning as a machine.

Is that unhappy?

I could not produce an answer.

Only one thing I knew. Unhappy or happy, the machine goes on performing the single function it has been given.

Until it breaks.

かつて胸に去来しなかったわけではないが、明確に
言語化するのは今が初めてだった。
　その一問。器械は不幸であるか。

　人形は、きっと不幸であろう。
　人の形に整えられながら人になれないのだから。

　しかし器械はどうか。
　器械として作られ器械として機能する器械。

　それは不幸であるのか。
　
　俺には答えを出せなかった。

　わかる事は一つきりだ。
　それが不幸であろうと幸福であろうと、器械は己に
与えられた単一機能を果たし続ける。

　壊れるまでずっと。

About half a century ago, in Europe, there was a movement to build a nation upon an idea called <ruby>communism<rt>communism</rt></ruby>. Break with capitalism, create a <ruby>completely<rt>complete</rt></ruby> equal society: that was the ideal. But the ideal was so far removed from reality that it could not even win the support of the poor it meant to save. From those in power, naturally, came repression. The movement has already perished.

Just before dying on the execution ground, its leader left a famous saying: if only this world had neither the <ruby>cross<rt>Crus</rt></ruby> nor <ruby>sword-armor<rt>Crus</rt></ruby>.
